chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibnasan, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the vegetables: the endive (al-hindaba'), the basil (al-badharuj), and the watercress (al-jarjir). He (peace be upon him) said: 'The endive and the basil are for us (the Ahl al-Bayt), and the watercress is for the Banu Umayya.'

key_terms.لَنَا: For us (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.لِبَنِي أُمَيَّةَ: For the Banu Umayya (the Umayyad clan)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the distinction between endive, basil, and watercress in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) assigns specific vegetables to the Ahl al-Bayt and the Banu Umayya, a tradition often interpreted through the lens of *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) where the qualities of the plants reflect the spiritual or political nature of their respective groups. While some scholars view this as a literal designation of ownership or consumption, others see it as a symbolic critique of the Umayyad dynasty's character, contrasting the purity of the Imams with the worldly nature of their rivals. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly practice of finding deep theological and historical insights in everyday matters (*al-awdah*).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ahmad Bin Suleyman, from his father, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘A man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the vegetable, the endive and the sweet basil and the watercress. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The endive and the sweet basil is for us<sup>asws</sup> and the watercress is for the Clan of Umayya’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Musa ibn al-Hassan from Ahmad ibn Sulayman from his father from abu Basir who has said the following: “
Once, a man asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about endives, sweet basil and watercress. He (the Imam) said, ‘Endives and sweet basil are for us and watercress is for banu ’Umayyah.’”
